# WW-003 — M1 fixture permission, truth, provenance and calibration/holdout protocol

**Record date:** 2026-10-04 · **Protocol author:** Lead · **Informational issue owner:** Pipeline · **Issue:** [WW-003 (#5)](https://github.com/brandonmartinez/WaveWrangler/issues/5) · **Milestone:** [M1](https://github.com/brandonmartinez/WaveWrangler/milestone/1)
**Registry:** [`fixtures/m1-fixture-registry.json`](fixtures/m1-fixture-registry.json) (`m1-fixtures-v5-frozen3`), generated by [`fixtures/generate-registry.py`](fixtures/generate-registry.py) · **Contracts:** [WW-009 record](ww-009-m1-contracts.md)

**Status:** FROZEN 2026-10-05 (`m1-freeze-1`, **retroactive**, see [§4.1](#41-freeze-record-m1-freeze-1-2026-10-05); `M1-DUR-025`: `m1-freeze-2` (§4.2) **failed** its holdout at 95/100 and is retained; it is superseded by `m1-freeze-3`, see [§4.3](#43-freeze-revision-m1-freeze-3-2026-10-05-m1-dur-025-supersedes-m1-freeze-2)) / PRE-FREEZE RUNS DISCLOSED / POST-FREEZE HOLDOUT PENDING. This defines what M1 evidences and how; this record claims **no** fixture result. Results are reported in the PRs and the M1 exit record. WW-003's M1 staged closure ([live issue](https://github.com/brandonmartinez/WaveWrangler/issues/5)) requires this complete M1-applicable registry/protocol **plus** the per-family freeze records and executed evidence. Later M2–M4 qualification stays in its domain issues (§8).

**Counts are generated, not hand-summed.** `python3 docs/m1/fixtures/generate-registry.py` writes the registry and prints its `counts`; `--check` exits non-zero if the committed JSON differs from the script. The script asserts complete fields, unique IDs, ≥100 holdout per boundary, the DUR-006 cell arithmetic and WW-006 ≥1,000. Every number in §2/§5/§6 is copied from that output.

## 1. Basis

- [Shared fixture and calibration protocol](../planning/research.md#shared-fixture-and-calibration-protocol): go with 100% permission/provenance/truth; otherwise synthetic-only and block unrepresented claims; controlled pre-holdout calibration; weaker gates need explicit Lead/Brandon approval.
- Historical foundation protocols (seed 20261004; 5,897 primary recipes / 169 calibration / 5,728 primary holdout) and the project-format batch (6,410 assertions) remain **historical** and are not reused, rerun or relabelled as M1 evidence ([foundation](../research/foundation-spikes.md#ww-003-fixture-truth-and-provisional-gate-contract), [project format](../research/project-format-recovery.md#qualification-accounting)). The M1 registry uses a new seed derivation and new IDs.

## 3. Generation, truth and provenance rules

1. **Determinism:** case seed = `sha256("ww-m1-fixture|v1|" + fixtureId + "|" + split + "|" + caseIndex)` → first 8 bytes big-endian UInt64. Calibration and holdout seeds differ by `split`; IDs are disjoint by construction.
2. **Location:** generated inside a per-run temporary directory created by the test harness and deleted afterwards — never in the repository, user home folders or the app's real container. Exceptions: `M1-SCALE-001` artifacts may persist under the worktree's gitignored `.build/` during a run; grant-C runs use only `WaveWrangler-M1-Synthetic-Trial` and delete it afterwards (deletion recorded).
3. **Content:** "source" files are random bytes with audio-like extensions; nothing decodes, header-reads or previews them. The **harness** (outside the app under test) may digest them to prove zero source writes (`M1-REF-018`); the **app** never hashes sources.
4. **Truth independence:** expected truth is declared in the registry and constructed by test code from the recipe, not from the code under test's output. Callback success never counts as truth; truth is independently read-back disk state, gateway call log, scope counter or harness digest.
5. **Provenance:** each entry records author/date, generator owner (the lane writing it) and, when frozen, generator source hash and freeze record path.
6. **Privacy:** no personal file names, paths or content appear in fixtures, committed logs or PR text.

## 4. Calibration, freeze and holdout

- **Calibration** may tune only non-gate implementation parameters (e.g., retry backoff, debounce within the ≤2 s gate, buffer sizes, harness timeouts) and fix harness bugs. Gate values and truth definitions are never tuned.
- **Freeze record (per family, before first holdout case):** dated JSON committed alongside evidence: fixture ID(s), registry version, generator source hash, recipe, truth definition, calibration results summary, holdout count, gate, host (`sw_vers`, `xcodebuild -version`, cores, memory), commit SHA.
- **Holdout** runs once per frozen revision; every case reported, including failures/exclusions/abstentions. A failure is fixed by a **new** frozen revision with fresh holdout; the failed run is retained, never overwritten.
- **Counts** may increase before freeze; never below a frozen gate minimum (≥100 per boundary, ≥1,000 WW-006 lifecycle, 100 projects/1,000 references) without explicit Lead/Brandon approval.
- **Timing statistics:** nearest-rank p95 = value at rank `ceil(0.95 × n)`; report first-open and warm separately; always report maximum.

### 4.1 Freeze record `m1-freeze-1` (2026-10-05)

The machine-readable record is the registry's top-level `freeze` object; this section summarizes it.

- **Scope:** all 58 `authorized-synthetic` and `authorized-user-grant` entries — IDs, recipes, truth, splits, gates and claim limits exactly as in the registry. Not-authorized entries freeze only after exact consent. `M1-USER-001` is manual and non-statistical, so it is not frozen.
- **Base:** `main` at `7087aa3` (the PR #60 merge). The freeze takes effect at the merge commit of the PR that adds it.
- **Generator sources:** git tree IDs at the base for the pre-freeze test harness (`WWSourcesTests`, `WWPersistenceTests`, `WWPersistenceProbe`, `WWOrganizerTests`, `WWCoreTests`, `WaveWranglerTests`, `WaveWranglerUITests`), verifiable with `git rev-parse 7087aa3:<path>`. The frozen **definition** is each entry's recipe, truth, split and gate; post-freeze runs report the tree IDs they actually ran.
- **Changes at freeze:** no gate, truth or count changed from `m1-fixtures-v2-draft`. One entry was added: `M1-SRC-ON-002-REVIEW` (10 / 100), which already ran on `main` after the PR #54 review. It does not count toward the WW-006 ≥1,000 reference total.
- **Deviation (disclosed):** the protocol was defined at the PR #51 merge but was **not frozen before execution**. Runs reported in PRs #54, #56, #57, #58 and #60 used the seeded derivation without a dated freeze record. They are labelled **pre-freeze**, retained unchanged and never relabelled as holdout.
- **Post-freeze rule:** a run counts as post-freeze holdout only on a commit that contains this record's merge commit, reported with commit SHA, host, every case and actual counts. Harness counts may exceed the frozen minimums, never fall below them. New harness code that implements a frozen definition at its frozen counts (loops, parameterized tests) does not change the definition. Changing a frozen recipe, truth, count or gate needs a new dated freeze revision with fresh holdout. Pre-freeze runs serve as the calibration record; post-freeze runs report holdout only, and any extra calibration is reported separately and never tunes gates or truth.

### 4.2 Freeze revision `m1-freeze-2` (2026-10-05, `M1-DUR-025`)

The machine-readable record is the registry's `freezeRevisions[0]`.

- **Trigger:** user grant E (2026-10-05), given directly: "yes, you can do multi-device icloud testing. ui stays on the mac mini".
- **Scope:** `M1-DUR-025` only. Every `m1-freeze-1` entry is unchanged.
- **Made before any holdout execution.** Disclosed: while this freeze was in review, a development smoke run of the two-host harness ran 1 case per cell (synthetic; not calibration, not holdout, not counted). It found P0 [#117](https://github.com/brandonmartinez/WaveWrangler/issues/117): an iCloud library conflict version was never surfaced. That led to the explicit detection mechanism in truths 1–2. Truth was tightened, never loosened; counts are unchanged. Base is `main` at `251d122`; the revision takes effect at the merge commit of its PR.
- **Hosts:**
  - Host A is this Mac (main).
  - Host B is the Mac mini.
  - Both run only the headless harness, so there's no app GUI on host A.
  - Every run record labels both hosts.
- **Cells (calibration / holdout):**
  - show-conflict 3 / 30: two-host publish race on one show;
  - library-conflict 3 / 30: two-host race on one library;
  - cross-machine-relink 2 / 20: sources created on A, opened on B with no access record, then an explicit regrant; variants are same, moved and same-name replaced;
  - recovery 2 / 20: B holds unpublished edits while A publishes, B relaunches, or A is killed at P4/P5.
- **Truth:**
  1. **Conflict detection:** at most one host is acknowledged per base, and detection follows a stated mechanism.
     - **Shows:** whenever the provider produces an unresolved NSFileVersion conflict version, it is surfaced as evidence (C4, no automatic merge) and never silently resolved. The count, including zero, is visible in the show status. Any show race loses no edit, either through the app's base-check stop with the losing candidate preserved, or through a surfaced provider version.
     - **Library:** whenever an unresolved provider conflict version exists, it is detected on load, on reload and before each update, and drives L4 (`changedElsewhere`). An app-detected divergence also drives L4.
     - A provider conflict version that is never surfaced is a failure. Whether provider versions exist is reported, never assumed.
  2. **Preservation:**
     - **Shows:** both edits are preserved in the canonical file, the losing host's candidate, or a surfaced conflict version.
     - **Library:** in every race, whatever triggered L4 (a provider version or app detection), after L4 → Combine (ST-36) both Macs' changes are in the current library on **both** hosts. When provider conflict versions exist, each is backed up to the device-local recovery store before it is marked resolved. Concurrent Combines converge.
  3. **No mixed revisions:** every reopen on either host is whole and valid, or an honest refusal.
  4. **NSFileVersion:** current, unresolved-conflict and other version counts are observed and reported per case per host.
  5. **Relink:** needs an explicit regrant. Never resolved by path or name, and never a silent substitution. Zero source writes on both hosts.
  6. **Recovery:** unpublished work stays recoverable on the host that made it. No cross-device recovery is claimed, and nothing shows as Saved without a read-back.
  7. **Atomicity:** no provider-atomicity claim follows from any result.
- **Claim limits:** iCloud Drive, two Macs, one account, synthetic files only. Sync timing is uncontrolled and is reported as observed. The harness is unsandboxed, so the regrant is a harness-supplied explicit choice, not the powerbox panel (the sandboxed grant is `M1-REF-020`).
- **Post-freeze rule:** as in §4.1.
  - Holdout counts only on a clean commit that contains this revision's merge.
  - It runs once and reports every case, including timeouts.
  - Each run records both hosts and the harness tree IDs.
  - Calibration is reported separately and tunes nothing.

#### 4.2.1 Interpretation note for `M1-DUR-025` truth 1 (Lead, 2026-10-05; recorded before any holdout case)

**Question.** In a provider-level race, both Macs can publish, read back and show C3's local acknowledgement "Saved on this Mac — revision r+1" before iCloud picks a winner. Truth 7 says nothing is atomic at the provider. Read literally, truth 1's "at most one host's publication is acknowledged as the current revision" would fail every provider race by construction.

**Ruling: an interpretation, not a truth change.**
- C3 separates **local** acknowledgement ("Saved on this Mac", local coherent disk truth) from provider state ("Provider sync: unknown", which a local save never implies).
- "Acknowledged as the current revision" in truth 1 therefore means a **cross-device** claim that a publication is the current revision. A local "Saved on this Mac" during the race is not one.
- Truth 1 is judged at the **settle point** the recipe already defines ("wait until both hosts observe a stable file", bounded; timeout = case failure).
- The registry entry, counts and gates are unchanged. No `M1-DUR-025` holdout case has run.

**Per case, all of these must hold (show and library cells):**
1. **One current publication.** After settle, exactly one publication is current, and both hosts read the same whole valid revision (byte-identical canonical file, checksum valid).
2. **Every other acknowledged publication is accounted for.** After settle, each other host's locally acknowledged publication is either:
   - **app-detected:** the base check stopped it as Conflict, with the losing candidate preserved; or
   - **provider-surfaced:** it exists as an unresolved provider conflict version that the app surfaces. For shows, that means a nonzero conflict count in the show's status (C4). For the library, it means L4, then Combine as in truth 2.
   - A losing publication that is neither app-detected nor provider-surfaced (silent last-writer-wins) is a **failure**. That is the #117 class.
3. **No false claim.**
   - No host ever shows a cross-device, "synced" or "current everywhere" claim for a losing publication.
   - After settle, a losing host never keeps showing an unqualified "Saved" for it without a conflict indication: Conflict, a show conflict count, or library L4.
   - "Saved on this Mac" during the race is permitted, because it is local truth.
4. **Library.** After settle, the library is never in L1 ("ready") on a host that holds an unsurfaced conflict version, and truth 2 (Combine, then both Macs' changes current on both hosts, with a backup before resolve) holds.
5. **Reported per case**, as evidence, not as gates:
   - the number of hosts that showed a local acknowledgement;
   - time from the trigger to settle;
   - time to surfacing (app-detected or provider-surfaced) on each host;
   - provider conflict and other version counts on each host;
   - which detection path fired.

**Why this doesn't loosen truth 1.** Truth 1 still bans unsurfaced loss, cross-device false claims and mixed revisions. The note adds stricter after-settle requirements (3–4), adds no exclusions and changes no counts. Had a requirement been relaxed, it would have needed a new freeze revision (`m1-freeze-3`) before holdout.

### 4.3 Freeze revision `m1-freeze-3` (2026-10-05, `M1-DUR-025`; supersedes `m1-freeze-2`)

The machine-readable record is the registry's `freezeRevisions[1]`, together with `M1-DUR-025.recipeFreeze3` and the cells' `variantsFreeze3`.

**Why a new revision.** The `m1-freeze-2` holdout ran once at `8456bcd` and **failed at 95/100**:

| Cell | Result |
| --- | --- |
| show-conflict | 30/30 |
| library-conflict | 30/30 |
| cross-machine-relink | **15/20** |
| recovery | 20/20 |

- **The 5 relink failures (cases 61–65) were setup stalls.** A third generated source never reached host B within 3 × 420 s while those cases set up concurrently with other cells. No product truth was evaluated in them, and the cause was not determined.
- **The independent review of the evidence ([#128](https://github.com/brandonmartinez/WaveWrangler/pull/128)) found four more gaps:**
  - Host B's library level was not sampled while B held an unresolved conflict version.
  - The run record lacked `xcodebuild -version`.
  - Neither concurrent Combine nor the app-level base-check path for shows was exercised.
  - P1 [#131](https://github.com/brandonmartinez/WaveWrangler/issues/131): the Combine message reports an ST-36-kept reorder as "couldn't be combined".
- **The failed run is retained** as `m1-freeze-2`'s result. It is never relabelled, and its seeds are not reused for counted cases.

**Unchanged:** counts and cells (10 / 100; show 3/30, library 3/30, relink 2/20, recovery 2/20), the hosts, the trial folder and every other registry entry.

**Truths: unchanged or tighter.**
1. **§4.2.1 folded in.** The interpretation is now part of truth 1 in the registry text. There is no wording change in substance.
2. **Level sampling on both hosts.**
   - **Ordering gate:** in every library case, host A's Combine waits until host B has observed the unresolved version (or app-detected L4). B must record at least two level samples while holding it, the first within 5 s of observing it. In the concurrent variant, both hosts must meet the gate before round 1.
   - **Sampling:** each host samples through the read-only load path (`lib-inspect`) at least every 5 s and at every load, until resolution.
   - **FAIL:** any ready/L1 sample on a host while `NSFileVersion.unresolvedConflictVersionsOfItem` for the library is non-empty there.
3. **Concurrent Combine.** The library cell has variants `combineOnAThenB` (20) and `concurrentCombine` (10).
   - **Rounds:** round 1 runs Combine on both hosts at a shared trigger. Any later rounds run on host A only, with at most 3 rounds and a 600 s settle each.
   - **Converged:** one current library, byte-identical on both hosts, containing every seeded edit (ST-36 copies count as carried), with 0 unresolved versions on either host and every resolved version backed up.
   - Anything else is a **failure**.
4. **Show app-level path.** The show cell has variants `simultaneous` (20) and `staggered` (10).
   - **Staggered:** B opens revision r and holds it. A publishes r+1. The bounded wait for r+1 to reach B runs inside the product phase, so if it expires the case **fails**. B then publishes from the stale base.
   - **Expected:**
     - a C3 base-check Conflict on B;
     - B's candidate preserved;
     - B never shows Saved;
     - A's r+1 current and byte-identical on both hosts.
5. **Combine-summary honesty (#131).** Per case, the summary's carried and not-carried items must equal the sets computed from the library models before and after. This fails until #131 is fixed.

**Recipe additions (frozen in advance; persistence-lane numbers accepted by Lead):**
- **Setup preconditions:**
  - A case is *established* only when, **strictly before its first product operation**:
    - host A's setup publication completed successfully (C3 steps 1–8, acknowledged and read back on A); and
    - host B has observed every setup fixture with the expected digest or publication ID.
  - If a fixture is still missing on B after a 420 s wait, B calls `startDownloadingUbiquitousItem` on that synthetic fixture and waits one more 420 s (worst case 840 s).
  - **`setupNotEstablished` is reserved for a fixture that has not arrived.** At expiry, the fixture is absent on B (or only a dataless placeholder), host A holds it readable with the expected digest, and A's setup publication succeeded. No product truth is evaluated, and the case is neither a pass nor a fail.
  - **Every other setup outcome is a case failure:**
    - the fixture is present on B with a wrong digest or publication ID;
    - the fixture isn't readable on A with the expected digest;
    - A's setup publication failed, was refused, or is acknowledgement-uncertain;
    - a wait's expiry is not strictly earlier than the first product operation.
  - **Diagnostics at every expiry, on both hosts:**
    - the local digest, or absence;
    - presence, size and dataless state;
    - A's uploaded/uploading state;
    - B's downloading status and any download error;
    - A's setup publication outcome and acknowledgement state.
  - The case folder is deleted only at the end of the run, after diagnostics.
  - Relink truth 5 (zero source writes) is checked for `setupNotEstablished` cases too.
  - Any timeout after the first product operation is still a **case failure**.
- **First product operation (named per cell/variant):**

  | Cell / variant | First product operation |
  | --- | --- |
  | show `simultaneous` | each host's open of revision r |
  | show `staggered` | host B's open of r, which it then holds |
  | library (both variants) | the first product library load on either host |
  | relink | host B's open of the show |
  | recovery | host B's first edit on r |

  Every case records, on both hosts, the first-product-operation timestamp and each setup wait's start and expiry (host clocks plus the measured A–B offset).
- **Replacement, never lowering the count:**
  - A `setupNotEstablished` slot is refilled from the frozen reserve split `holdout-f3-reserve`. Indices are used in order, with the same cell and variant, and recorded per slot.
  - Refills continue until each cell has evaluated exactly its frozen holdout count.
  - If `setupNotEstablished` exceeds **20%** of a cell, the cell **fails as incomplete**: more than 6 cases for show or library, more than 4 for relink or recovery.
- **Concurrency:** at most one case is in setup at a time, across all cells. At most 6 product workers run at once.
- **Host labels, on both hosts.** Hosts are identified only as "host A" and "host B". No hostname, computer name or account identifier is recorded, because macOS default names can embed the account's full name.
  - hardware model, CPU, cores and memory, and `sw_vers` product and build;
  - `xcodebuild -version`, `xcrun --show-sdk-version` and `swift --version`;
  - the sha256 of the probe binary run (it must match between hosts);
  - the commit SHA and harness tree IDs;
  - "same Apple account: operator-attested", with no account identifiers.
  - A run missing any label, or with mismatched probe hashes, is **invalid**.
- **Per-case reporting.** §4.2.1 condition 5 still applies to every case, as evidence, not gates: local acknowledgements, time to settle, time to surfacing per host, version counts per host and the detection path. `m1-freeze-3` adds these per case:
  - variant and setup outcome, including diagnostics;
  - reserve index;
  - first-product-operation and wait timestamps on both hosts;
  - level samples on both hosts;
  - Combine rounds;
  - Combine-summary sets against the harness-computed sets.
- **Seeds:** fresh splits `calibration-f3`, `holdout-f3` and `holdout-f3-reserve`.
- **Calibration coverage:** the 10 calibration cases include at least one staggered show case, one `concurrentCombine` case and one case that exercises the host-B sampling gate. In addition, a forced `setupNotEstablished` drill, using an injected unreachable fixture, tests the retry, the diagnostics and the reserve refill. It is reported separately and is not one of the 10.

**Note on the setup reclassification.** Under `m1-freeze-2`, a setup stall was a case failure. Under `m1-freeze-3`, it is reported with diagnostics and replaced, within a 20% cap. This changes how *non-product* setup stalls are classified. Only a fixture that **has not arrived**, with host A's side verified, before the first product operation qualifies. It is frozen **before** any new run and does not touch any product truth. A stall after the product phase begins is still a failure, and the evaluated count can never fall below the frozen count.

**Post-freeze rule:** as in §4.2. It runs once, on a clean commit containing this revision's merge. Calibration (`calibration-f3`) is reported separately and tunes nothing.

## 5. M1 strata and planned counts

Full fields are in the registry. Counts are **calibration / holdout**.

### Publication boundaries (derived from [WW-009 C3](ww-009-m1-contracts.md#c3--save-ordering-publication-and-acknowledgement-d))

| Show boundary | After → before | Public injection point | Paths |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| P1 | candidate validated → prior retained | publisher hook; NSDocument `writeSafely` override before `super` | publisher + NSDocument |
| P2 | prior retained → coordinated write/base check | publisher hook; `writeSafely` override before `super` | publisher + NSDocument |
| P3 | base check passed → bytes written | coordinator accessor; throw from `write(to:ofType:for:originalContentsURL:)` override | publisher + NSDocument |
| P4 | staged bytes flushed → canonical replace | publisher stage → `replaceItemAt` | **publisher only** (no public hook inside AppKit `writeSafely`) |
| P5 | publication returned → read-back | publisher hook; `writeSafely` override after `super` | publisher + NSDocument |
| P6 | read-back verified → library ack | save-completion handler | publisher + NSDocument |
| P7 | library ack → index update | index updater entry | publisher + NSDocument |

| Library boundary | After → before | Injection point |
| --- | --- | --- |
| L1 | library candidate validated → prior retained | library publisher hook |
| L2 | prior retained → coordinated write | library publisher hook |
| L3 | base check passed → stage write | coordinator accessor |
| L4 | stage flushed → `replaceItemAt` | library publisher hook |
| L5 | publish returned → read-back | library publisher hook |
| L6 | read-back verified → index update | index updater entry |

**NSDocument-path evidence limit:** P1–P3 and P5–P7 are deterministic on both paths; P4 is deterministic only for the WWPersistence publisher. The NSDocument path reaches P4 only through non-deterministic process kills (reported separately in `M1-DUR-021`) and supports only "AppKit stock safe-save, not independently interrupted".

## 7. Supported-claim limits

- Synthetic evidence supports only the represented local strata **on the claimed host** (macOS 27.0.1, Xcode 27, 18-core Apple silicon, 128 GiB).
- Grant-A/B/D runs are scripted or single-operator runs on this host — not participant usability or reference-device evidence (WW-052).
- Grant-C results support "iCloud Drive, one trial folder, this Mac" only — not OneDrive/Dropbox, two-device sync, provider atomicity in general or power loss.
- No qualification of real media/formats, Developer ID/notarized/clean-install grants (WW-041/052) or the macOS 26/16 GB reference. A zero-failure finite set is not a universal guarantee.
